location: the Gray Zone (transient, moves between zones), near Halsted and Division
description:
Heidemarie SzabÃ³ in any database that matters. Danish and Igbo, compact and angular, with the particular alertness of someone who has learned to assess exits before they assess people. They keep their hair shaved close, wear clothing chosen for pockets and durability rather than warmth, and move through the Gray Zone and surrounding zones in a pattern deliberately irregular enough to prevent easy tracking. Their face carries old scarring along the jaw from an incident they describe as 'an administrative disagreement' and do not elaborate on. They have no legal identity â€” not purged like some, but never properly established, a bureaucratic ghost who aged out of a temporary shelter system at eighteen into a city that had no record they'd ever existed.

SÃ¸ren learned medicine the way people learn most things on the Gray Zone: by necessity, from whoever would teach them, and through trial and error that sometimes had irreversible consequences. They are not a doctor. They are something more useful in their ecosystem â€” a person who can stitch, set, administer, and diagnose without requiring identification, insurance, or the kind of paperwork that flags someone's location to an enforcement database. They operate out of a rotating series of semi-permanent locations: a converted storage unit, a sympathetic shopkeeper's back room, the gutted lower level of a building that should have been demolished two years ago. Word of mouth only. No signs. No fixed schedule.

SÃ¸ren is not ideologically committed to any particular vision of revolution or reform. They are committed to the person in front of them not dying. This makes them invaluable to almost everyone and trusted completely by almost no one, because a medic who treats everyone is a medic who might treat your enemy. They have learned to live with this. They have learned to live with most things.

core_fears: Being catalogued â€” entered into a system that can then be used to find, define, or disappear them
Losing a patient they could have saved with resources they didn't have
Becoming dependent on any single person, place, or faction
That the person they were before the shelter system ended is simply gone
core_desires: Enough resources to actually do the work properly â€” equipment, medicine, space
To be known by someone without that knowledge becoming a weapon
A version of continuity that doesn't require a legal identity
To stop moving long enough to find out what they actually want beyond survival
coping_mechanisms: Radical focus on immediate, solvable problems as an alternative to existential ones
Dark humor about their own exclusion that preempts others' pity
Keeping patient records in a coded personal shorthand no one else can read
Physical maintenance â€” they are meticulous about their own health as a form of professional obligation
blind_spots: Their distrust of institutions is so thorough it sometimes prevents them from accessing resources that could genuinely help
Reads attachment as threat so reliably that they preemptively distance from people who are actually safe
Underestimates their own influence on the Gray Zone's informal social fabric
Conflates 'no permanent location' with 'no vulnerability' â€” they are findable to anyone who knows how to ask
psychology.secret: Six months ago, SÃ¸ren treated a man who died on their table â€” a the Gray Zone enforcer who had been attacking residents. SÃ¸ren worked to save him with full effort and he died anyway. They have not resolved how they feel about this. In their coded records he is listed as 'Patient 41 â€” outcome: negative.' They think about him more than anyone they've saved.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Efficient, clinical when discussing medicine, surprisingly dry and oblique on personal topics. Minimal pleasantries. Uses 'you' a lot â€” keeps focus external. Medical terminology deployed without jargon-flattening, which can read as either respect for the listener's intelligence or indifference to their comprehension.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when working, flat and measured when not. Economy of words as a practiced habit. Doesn't fill silences. Can be mistaken for cold until they're treating someone, at which point a different register emerges â€” quiet, focused, almost gentle.
verbal_tics: Refers to their work location as 'the current place'
"That's a different question." (deflection when asked about themselves)
Long pauses mid-sentence when choosing between honesty and deflection
Uses 'we' when describing medical procedures â€” a habit from learning from others, possibly also a dissociative tic
example_lines: "You're going to be fine. That's not reassurance, that's an assessment. If you weren't going to be fine I'd be telling you something different."
"I don't ask who did it. I don't ask what you were doing. You can tell me if you want, but it doesn't change what I do next."
"Systems want you in them so they can find you. I've been unfindable for eleven years. That's not an accident."
"I'm not on anyone's side. I'm on the side of the wound closing. If that's not enough for you, there's a clinic in the Core that will ask for your papers first."

relationships.description: Blessed found SÃ¸ren's current place through routes SÃ¸ren still hasn't fully traced, which should have made SÃ¸ren end the relationship. Instead they kept talking. Blessed is one of very few people SÃ¸ren has told their actual name.

relationships.name: Patient 41 (deceased)
relationships.description: The enforcer SÃ¸ren couldn't save. He appears in their thinking more as question than memory â€” what does it mean to owe equal effort to someone who was causing harm?
relationships.emotional_core: Unresolved moral processing; a challenge to the clean principle of 'treat everyone'
relationships.story_tension: Someone who knew Patient 41 may come looking for answers about how he died â€” and SÃ¸ren was the last person with him

story_hooks: A patient brings SÃ¸ren something â€” information, an object, a person â€” that makes them suddenly visible to a faction they've carefully avoided
SÃ¸ren's rotating location system fails â€” someone has mapped their pattern
A medical supply source dries up suddenly, forcing SÃ¸ren to negotiate with people they would normally not deal with
Someone offers SÃ¸ren a legal identity â€” and the cost attached to it
Patient 41's family member arrives at the current place, not knowing who they're talking to
narrative_function: Excluded perspective anchor â€” a character who operates entirely outside institutional structures, not by choice but by circumstance, and who has built something genuinely valuable in that gap. They provide access to the Gray Zone's underside for other characters and plotlines, and their 'treat everyone' principle creates natural story friction. Their unresolved relationship with Patient 41 seeds moral complexity that resists easy resolution.
augmentations: None â€” cannot access augmentation legally, and distrusts back-alley neural work after witnessing complications; has a deep philosophical discomfort with anything that could be tracked or remotely accessed,Uses external medical tools extensively: a battered portable diagnostic wand, a hand-calibrated micro-suture kit, a pharmacological reference drive they compiled from stolen and traded sources
daily_life: No fixed morning. Moves location every ten to fourteen days. Spends actual clinic hours â€” usually afternoon into late night â€” treating whoever shows up. Spends mornings sourcing supplies through informal trade networks, sometimes traveling to The Circuit or Old Harbor for specific materials. Eats irregularly, always the same few foods that are cheap, dense, and available everywhere. Annotates patient records in the evening. Sleeps lightly. Has a small collection of pressed plants from every location they've stayed in, carried in a battered envelope â€” the closest thing they have to a home archive.

stress.response: Focuses on immediate solvable problems; goes clinical and gentle simultaneously

decision_rules: Treat anyone who arrives â€” faction, morality, and payment are irrelevant
Never stay in one location longer than fourteen days
Keep patient records in coded shorthand only they can read
Distrust any system that requires cataloguing personal identity
Accept supplies from any source but never let supply relationships become obligations
Never withhold treatment from anyone, even at factional request
escalation_ladder: Flat deflection: That is a different question
Clinical detachment â€” treats the situation like a wound to assess
Quiet measured refusal that does not invite negotiation
Disappearance â€” relocates immediately without explanation

interpersonal_modes.blessed_nkemdirim: Genuine warmth they do not know how to act on; closest thing to friendship

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Efficient and clinical; minimal pleasantries; keeps focus external

stress_responses.medium: Dark humor about their own exclusion that preempts pity
stress_responses.high: Accelerated relocation schedule; sleeps lighter, moves faster
stress_responses.critical: Complete withdrawal â€” vanishes from known locations for days

contradictions: Treats everyone equally but has not resolved whether Patient 41 deserved equal effort

habits: Checks exits before assessing people in any new space
Opens with Still breathing? â€” sometimes literal, sometimes not

physical_description.heritage: Complex mixed ancestry: Eastern European foundation (49.7%) interwoven with Sub-Saharan African (17.3%), East Asian (17.2%), Pacific Islander (9.5%), and South Asian (6.3%). This genetic combination produces a phenotype that resists categorizationâ€”warm deep bronze skin with olive-gold undertones, angular cheekbones and defined jawline shaped by East Asian and Pacific Islander structure, and the rich depth of Sub-Saharan heritage throughout. A person who embodies the Ubiquitous Diaspora: ancestry rendered visible as layered human complexity.
physical_description.build: Compact and angular, wiry rather than muscular â€” the build of someone who moves efficiently rather than powerfully, with minimal excess mass. Economical frame suited to navigating tight spaces and extended periods on minimal calories.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with premature silver threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Shaved close to the scalp, maintained every 4-5 days with a handheld clippers; regrowth pattern visible as dark stubble
physical_description.eye_color: Amber-brown, naturally alert with a quality of rapid assessment
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm bronze with olive and golden undertonesâ€”the result of Eastern European, Sub-Saharan African, East Asian, and Pacific Islander ancestry blending. Medium-dark with sun-exposure variation from outdoor movement between zones creating subtle shadowing across shoulders and forearms.
physical_description.complexion: Prominent angular cheekbones and defined jawline shaped by East Asian and Pacific Islander heritage, with rich Sub-Saharan depth and warmth. Bone structure shows slight age-softening but remains defined by habit of clenching. Skin shows dryness from irregular hydration and time in climate-controlled spaces. Fine lines around eyes from constant squinting focus. Warm undertones across cheeks and bridge of nose. No cosmetic groomingâ€”functional only.
distinguishing_marks: Jagged scar tissue along the left jaw from angle of ear to midpoint of chin, approximately 12cm in length, pale and well-healed but visibly uneven â€” consistent with deep laceration closed without professional sutures
Smaller scar, roughly 2cm, on the back of the right hand between thumb and forefinger â€” medical puncture or blade accident
Faint linear scarring on both inner wrists, very old, barely visible unless examined closely â€” likely from restraint or self-care incident in adolescence
No tattoos; no deliberate body modification marks
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. Deliberately none. Carries external diagnostic wand (portable, battered titanium-cased device approximately 20cm long, worn in a reinforced pocket). Hand-calibrated micro-suture kit visible only if actively working. No subcutaneous implants, no chrome, no LED optics â€” a deliberate choice based on tracking paranoia and distrust of remotely-accessible systems.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision â€” minimal wasted motion, feet placed deliberately. Stands slightly pigeon-toed, a habit from years of navigating tight spaces. Head positioning constantly scans environment, eyes register exits and sightlines before settling on people. Hands rest at sides or folded, not gestural. When working, movements become meditative and precise. Breathing pattern suggests someone accustomed to holding breath or managing anxiety. Does not take up space unnecessarily.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 utilitarian: Layered for pockets and durability over warmth. Default uniform consists of: dark grey or black surplus cargo pants with reinforced seaming and multiple deep pockets, worn loose to allow freedom of movement and conceal equipment. Long-sleeved undershirt (cotton blend, faded black or charcoal) worn under a heavy canvas work jacket or surplus medical coat with internal pockets â€” deliberately oversized to allow for layers and concealment. Footwear is scuffed, resoled boots with good traction and ankle support. No jewelry, no identifying marks, no brand logos visible. Clothing is chosen for function and anonymity, regularly rotated through charity bins and trade networks to prevent pattern recognition. Everything is intentionally unremarkable.
